narrative_purpose: A naturalist gallery of four real Earth endosymbioses so the reader sees how common and varied live-in partnerships are, and where Spider fits among them.
subject: A four-panel specimen gallery, each a small vignette against dark ground: top-left, an aphid with a cluster of glowing rod-shaped bacteria packed into special cells in its abdomen; top-right, a small bobtail squid with a luminous oval light organ glowing on its underside; bottom-left, a coral polyp with tiny golden-green algae suspended inside its translucent tissue; bottom-right, a single-celled amoeba with a curved blue-green photosynthetic body held inside it.
scene: A gallery plate of four separate organisms, each showing its internal symbiont.
camera: A flat grid of four equal specimen vignettes, two over two.
light: Bioluminescent key within each organism from its symbiont — cyan, teal, and a restrained gold-green in the coral and amoeba; each vignette on its own pool of dark.
palette: Void-indigo base, Pandora cyan and living teal dominant, a small controlled warm gold-green confined to the coral's and amoeba's algae; dark separating margins.
style: Painterly speculative-biology naturalist plate, hand-painted texture, observed-from-life confidence, luminous and atmospheric.
detail_level: Crisp on each organism and its glowing internal symbiont; the four dark backgrounds kept plain.
composition: A clean two-by-two grid with dark gutters between panels for labels.
consistency_notes: Four distinct real Earth organisms, each clearly showing an internal glowing guest. Cool palette with tightly restrained warm only in the algal symbionts.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no logos, no diagram labels, no arrows, no leader lines, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares, no neon UI glow, no cartoon or anime style
